title: Expectancy, R and position size
subtitle: Read a trading scorecard like a quant

sections.title: R-multiples
beats: R is the amount you risk on a trade: entry to stop.
Measure every result in R. Made 2× what you risked = +2R. Got stopped = −1R.
Using R lets you compare a $5 trade to a $50 trade fairly.
sections.example: Risk $10 (stop $1 away, 10 units). Close $2.50 in profit per unit = +$25 = +2.5R.
sections.sayback: Explain why measuring in R beats measuring in dollars.
sections.tieback: A sensible go-live gate: positive average R over a decent sample of real trades.

sections.title: Expectancy & profit factor
beats: Expectancy = win rate × average win − loss rate × average loss. That's EV per trade.
Profit factor = total won ÷ total lost. Above 1 means you're net up.
Worked: 45% wins averaging +2R, 55% losses at −1R. Expectancy = 0.9 − 0.55 = +0.35R per trade.
sections.sayback: Say back: why can a 45% win rate be good?

quiz.q: Wins total $300, losses total $200. Profit factor?

sections.title: Position size from the stop
beats: Pick dollars at risk first. Then size = dollars at risk ÷ distance to stop.
A wider stop means a smaller position, so the dollar risk stays the same.
ATR stops: ATR (average true range, typical daily move) sets how far the stop sits. A good risk check rejects stops tighter than some multiple of ATR.
sections.example: Risk $2, ATR $0.40, mult 1.5 → stop $0.60 away → size ≈ 3.3 units.
sections.sayback: Explain why the stop decides size, not the other way round.
